failure_summary.description: The answer added a narrower event modifier despite the clue asking for the event name and the existing rule to return the generic class at the requested scope.
For a bare pair of names, the agent supplied their relationship instead of the shared affiliation foregrounded by the context.

patch.reasoning: The first miss is already covered by the rules on requested scope and minimal complete labels, so adding another rule would be redundant. The second exposes a gap for terse entity-pair prompts with no explicit predicate; a focused rule can help distinguish a context-supported shared identifier from an unasked relationship.

edits.content:
## Interpret Bare Entity-Pair Prompts
When a terse prompt lists two or more named entities without asking a relation, treat it as a lookup cue rather than assuming the answer is their relationship. Use the context to identify a shared named affiliation or canonical descriptor consistently attached to them (such as a country or organization), and return that label. Give the relationship only when the prompt asks how the entities are related or the context provides no better-supported shared identifier.
